institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature of Norway, the possibility to keep the builded relations close, and a good study environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Trondheim is an amazing city for students, there are so many opportunities to participate in different groups doesn't matter if you are into sports, debates, music everything. The city is also the perfect size, and a great combination of citylife, nature with the mountains right beside the city and also the sea surrounding the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think there was an overall good information on the webpage, but there were still a lot of things that wasn't specified. There were quite good respons from exchange office and a few teachers, but some teachers never responded.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had different zoom meetings with overall information to international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We didn't get the social introduction due to corona, and although Norway opened, and they had promised to try making the event later, unfortunately that never happened.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I don't think it was that easy. There is a lot of house share options, but it is really difficult to get a sense of the vibe when you can't come see the room and meet people.  I ended up living at Singsaker Studenthome right down the street from NTNU and it is an awesome place if you love to be social.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
If you wan't to live with other exchange student go for the SIT appartements in Moholt, but if you are more interested in the norwegian experience be open to the different housings types and look at facebook pages or the webpage
hybel.no

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is quite strange that you are left on your own when you are a scandinavian when everybody else get help to find accommodation. 
Puts a big stressfactor on the us as students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The page was quite easy to use, and there was information on how to use.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was just filling out some form. The signing up for courses was a bit chaotic. Apparently you could sing up for as many as you wanted and then just withdrawal from those you didn't need afterwards.  It was your own responsibility to secure that the courses didn't overlap and that the exams wasn't on the same dates, and these informations was given quite late.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mailing with both NTNU exchange and the KU exchange people and a few professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress with it from home. Everything you try to plan from home will probably be changes when you arrive, so just relax. Also sign up for a lot of courses at NTNU and get a lot of prior approval from KU so you don't need to send in new versions 1000 times.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses was overall good. Unfortunately a lot was held online still although Norway had opened up and we had requested on campus lectures.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took one BA course the rest was MA but I was quite easy to follow.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar with lectures on MA level and more class attendance and group work on my BA course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BI2080 Global Change Biology 
MOL3018 Medical Toxicology
MOL3020 Virology
MOL3021 Bioinformatics - Applied Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The bioinformatics is an intense 2 week course and then an assignment - which give pretty much free time to do other fun stuff.

questions.answer: Memberships to sportorganisation, nice outdoor equipment, expensive roadboms

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and beer are expensive!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The membership of the sportsorganisation NTNUi give so many opportunities. A nice thing to know is that there are few spots on the different trips, so it can be nice to involve your self in the different clubs (be obs in the beginning of the semester)  Samfundet also has a lot of great cultural activities and here you can be a member as well and work as a volunteer.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be a volunteer - it creates network !

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Ski touring, crosscountry in bymarka, works in the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was more difficult than I imagined, but keep an open mind and give the Norwegians a few beers, then you are good to go.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
They are very helpfull and engage in social groups and volunteer work.
They love danish, but it is nice to shift a few words to Norwegian so they understand you better

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I experienced that they are a bit more traditional and reserved, but keep talking and taking initiative then they come around

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Keep an open mind! Don't be afraid to join things where you don't know anybody, because there will be so many other people in the same situation as you. 
Accept that it is a process and there will be days where you feel like you are a long way from home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Us the city and the universities initiatives!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be on my own and overcoming challenges. Also getting to know a city so well and experience another culture on close hand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being content and not thinking too much

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy! Rather do too many things than regret, and allow your self to pull the plug some times.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
